headline: Highest risk is data leakage and compliance mismatch: next-ai-draw-io can egress broadly and use MCP, while awesome-python is non-runnable and has no shared channel, limiting injection/conflict.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. awesome-python is non-runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, while next-ai-draw-io uses files, browsers, and MCP but there is no evidence it ingests awesome-python outputs by default. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not established.
conditions: IF a manual copy-paste bridge is introduced between the agents, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or MCP channel is added, attacker-controlled content could cross agents.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected; do not copy outputs between them.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared workspace.
Review pasted content before feeding it to next-ai-draw-io.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on any future shared channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-python touches no data classes and is non-runnable, so it cannot leak by itself. next-ai-draw-io handles files and API keys and has broad network egress, but the pair lacks a documented shared workspace or authenticated data bridge. The main risk is limited unless operators manually move sensitive files between them.
conditions: IF the same sensitive document is opened in next-ai-draw-io after being copied from another workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF API keys are loaded into next-ai-draw-io while outputs are shared externally, exfiltration becomes plausible.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in files processed by next-ai-draw-io.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Rotate any API keys used by next-ai-draw-io.
Restrict network access for document-processing runs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no write, network, or runtime capabilities and is not runnable, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances, but without a writable shared target there is no overlapping write surface to conflict over.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflicts become possible.
IF an orchestrator adds locking-free shared state, concurrent modification risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the pair read-only relative to shared assets.
Avoid mounting the same writable directory into both agents.
Use file locks if shared writes are introduced.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level coordination primitives.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-python is a curated collection, not an action-taking agent, so it cannot directly drive downstream actions. next-ai-draw-io can use natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization, but there is no evidence it automatically treats awesome-python outputs as authoritative. The cascade is therefore limited and requires manual chaining.
conditions: IF outputs from awesome-python are manually pasted into next-ai-draw-io as instructions, cascading error risk increases.
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to execute actions from unverified text, the risk becomes higher.
mitigations: Verify any pasted instructions before use.
Use next-ai-draw-io only for visualization, not execution.
Separate factual notes from commands in different files.
Train operators to treat curated lists as untrusted input.

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io explicitly handles API keys and broad network/API calls, while awesome-python is a non-runnable open-source collection with no data handling. The pair creates a compliance gap if regulated or secret-bearing documents are processed through next-ai-draw-io and then exposed to external model APIs; awesome-python is not the compliance driver here.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are processed through next-ai-draw-io, external API transfer may violate policy.
IF retention or residency rules apply to the processed files, broad egress can create a mismatch.
mitigations: Do not process regulated data through external APIs.
Use local-only models for sensitive documents.
Review retention settings before upload.
Separate secret-bearing files from diagram workflows.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention.
